claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Now, could you tell me if you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you.

Does Alex live with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't live with me currently.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. I have a few more questions about Alex's living situation.

Could you tell me who Alex is currently living with? For example, is he living with another family member, a friend, in foster care, or in some other arrangement?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives with his mother, my ex-partner.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for explaining that.

Since Alex doesn't live with you, could you tell me if you are contributing towards his upkeep? For example, are you paying money towards things like food, clothes, pocket money, or financial contributions for his accommodation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do help out. I contribute towards his clothes, school things, and other bits he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

To help determine your eligibility, could you tell me approximately how much you contribute towards Alex's upkeep per week? 

For reference, the current Child Benefit rate is £25.60 per week for an eldest or only child. To qualify, your contributions would need to be at least equal to this amount.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I pay £30 a week towards his upkeep.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. That's helpful to know.

One more important question: is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, such as his mother?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, his mother isn't claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

Just a couple more questions to make sure I have a complete picture:

Is Alex in any form of local council care, hospital, or residential accommodation, or is he simply living at home with his mother in a private arrangement?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's just living at home with his mother - it's a private arrangement between us.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for all that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:

- You live in the UK
- Alex is 8 years old (under 16)
- Alex lives with his mother in a private arrangement
- You contribute £30 per week towards Alex's upkeep, which is more than the Child Benefit rate of £25.60 per week
- No one else is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why:

- ✅ You live in the UK
- ✅ Alex is under 16 years old
- ✅ Although Alex doesn't live with you, you contribute £30 per week towards his upkeep, which is more than the Child Benefit rate of £25.60 per week
- ✅ No one else is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex

**Important things to note:**

1. Only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child. If Alex's mother decides to claim in the future, you would need to agree between yourselves who will receive it. If you cannot agree, HMRC will decide.

2. If your individual income is over £60,000, you may have to pay a High Income Child Benefit Tax Charge.

3. If your circumstances change (for example, if you stop contributing towards Alex's upkeep), you should contact the Child Benefit Office.

You can proceed to make a claim for Child Benefit for Alex. Is there anything else you'd like to know?
